subject: Legal jurisdiction affirmation + private connectivity checklist
messages:
From: Miguel Alvarez <miguel@healthspan.org>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: LegalOps <legalops@healthspan.org>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: Request: formal jurisdiction affirmation + private peering proof for EU-only deployment

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough today. As part of our procurement checklist for HealthSpan’s EU pilot, LegalOps needs two items before we can finalize the SOW:

1) A signed letter asserting that all customer data for the specified tenant will be hosted only in the EU region(s) specified (we listed Frankfurt and Dublin) and will not be replicated outside those regions except for encrypted backups with explicit customer consent.
2) Technical evidence that the private connectivity we discussed (VPC peering / PrivateLink / transit gateway) will terminate into a customer-controlled peering point in our EU VPC and that key materials (KMS/HSM) remain under our control or are partitioned per-tenant.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide both (1) and (2) and a short runbook describing the failover behavior if cross-region fallback is needed? We’d prefer to see diagrams and any SOC2/SIG attachments that substantiate the control paths.

Regards,
Miguel
Senior IT Contract Manager
HealthSpan

---
Note: LegalOps copied for timeline and contractual language alignment.

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Miguel Alvarez <miguel@healthspan.org>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 08:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: formal jurisdiction affirmation + private peering proof for EU-only deployment

Miguel,

Thanks — we can provide both items. High level:

- Residency affirmation: We will supply a signed residency boundary letter that states the customer’s production tenant will be served only from EU nodes (Frankfurt/Dublin) and that no customer plaintext data will be intentionally copied outside the EU without documented authorization. The letter will reference our data handling controls and fallback policies.

- Private connectivity proof: We’ll attach a network diagram showing the peering topology (Redwood-managed peering endpoints to your EU peering VPC) and a keystore inventory showing key partitioning. For KMS control: Redwood supports customer-managed keys (BYOK) in EU regions; we will detail whether keys are customer-owned HSM-backed or Redwood-managed with tenant separation.

Ben will drop the diagrams and the initial draft of the residency letter by today EOD. Grace will outline the failover runbook and the SLO / rollback behavior in the event an EU node becomes unavailable.

Next steps: Miguel — confirm the exact canonical account IDs for the HealthSpan peering VPC(s) and the preferred KMS workflow (BYOK or Redwood-managed CMKs). Once we have those, we can finalize the attachments for your LegalOps review.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Solutions - Redwood Inference
(attachment: none yet)

Miguel — attaching the requested artifacts for review.

Attachments:
- redwood_vpc_peering_diagram_v1.pdf (diagram: EU peering endpoints → transit gateway → customer VPC; annotated with IP ranges and NAT/egress paths)
- keystore_inventory_2026-07.csv (inventory: per-tenant key IDs, region, management mode: BYOK / Redwood-KMS, HSM-backed flag)
- residency_boundary_letter.pdf (draft letter; unsigned)

Quick notes:
- The peering diagram shows peering confined to eu-central-1 and eu-west-1. Cross-region replication for backups is opt-in and will only occur if you sign the disaster-recovery addendum.
- BYOK: we support customer-imported keys into an HSM in eu-central-1; we will include step-by-step import instructions and a minimal permissions policy.
- Transit fallback: we keep a standby routing policy that prefers same-region nodes. In a region outage, traffic can be routed to a warm standby node in the other EU region only after an automated health threshold is met and after the customer-configured failover window. Grace will add the exact threshold numbers in the runbook.

Please review and flag any legal phrasing changes you need. If LegalOps prefers, we can convert the residency letter to a short addendum to the SOW.

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood
(attachments: 3 files)

Thanks Ben — quick clarifications from LegalOps:

- In the residency letter we need explicit language about log storage locations (where access logs, application logs, audit trails are retained). Can Redwood confirm logs for the tenant are also retained only in the EU?
- For BYOK, we need confirmation on whether Redwood ever has administrative access to the imported keys (i.e., can Redwood export or unwrap customer-imported keys?). If there are any emergency access procedures, please call those out.

If you can update the CSV with the KMS management-mode column populated per-key and add a short paragraph to the residency letter addressing logs, that would be ideal.

Miguel

Miguel — thanks for the precise asks. I updated the runbook and residency letter draft to include the following items you requested:

- Logs: Application logs, access logs, audit trails tied to the tenant are retained in the EU and kept on regional storage buckets. We retain control-plane audit logs per SOC2 retention policy; these will be available for export on request and stored in eu-central-1 by default.
- BYOK emergency access: Customer-imported keys are imported into an HSM in your specified region. Redwood does not have the ability to export or unwrap customer-imported HSM keys; emergency access requires a documented process involving the customer key admin. We documented the emergency process in the addendum.
- I included a small section describing ephemeral cross-region caching for performance (read-only KV cache). That cache is encrypted and does not contain write-through replicas of customer data.

Attached: updated residency_boundary_letter.pdf (v2), updated keystore_inventory_2026-07.csv (marked management_mode per key), and a 2‑page runbook excerpt describing failover thresholds and notification procedures.

Grace O'Connor
Head of Product Ops, Redwood Inference
(attachments: updated letter, inventory, runbook excerpt)

Subject: Re: Request: formal jurisdiction affirmation + private peering proof for EU-only deployment

Thanks — Legal has reviewed the draft residency letter. A few editorial requests:

1) Replace ‘will not be replicated’ with ‘shall not be replicated’ and add a sentence clarifying that backups will remain encrypted and the customer must explicitly authorize cross-region transfer for disaster recovery.
2) Add a clause stating that Redwood will provide a 30-day notice before any change to the peering topology that could affect residency boundaries.

If you can produce the signed PDF with these edits and an updated keystore CSV, we can move to signatures on the SOW.

Best,
LegalOps (on behalf of HealthSpan)

Miguel — attaching the signed residency boundary letter (residency_boundary_letter.pdf, signed) and the updated keystore inventory (keystore_inventory_2026-07.csv) with management_mode populated. We also updated the letter language to the contractual phrasing LegalOps requested and added the 30-day notice clause for topology changes.

Summary of what’s enclosed:
- residency_boundary_letter.pdf (signed) — asserts EU-only hosting for the tenant, clarifies log storage locations, and states backups will not be replicated outside EU without explicit customer authorization; includes 30-day change notice clause.
- redwood_vpc_peering_diagram_v1.pdf — final diagram of peering endpoints and egress routes.
- keystore_inventory_2026-07.csv — per-key management_mode (BYOK / Redwood-KMS) and HSM flags; note: keys marked BYOK are customer-imported and Redwood cannot export or unwrap them.
- runbook excerpt (inline) — failover thresholds: automated failover triggers after 3 consecutive node health failures over 5 minutes, with a configurable 30–120 minute customer failover window before cross-region routing occurs. Notifications go to the on-call ops and the customer distribution list.

If LegalOps is satisfied, we can add these as SOW appendices and proceed to signature. Let me know if you need any additional SOC2 or SIG artifacts linked; we can provide a read-only Drive folder link to our compliance pack.

Thanks — looking forward to onboarding HealthSpan.
